midnight.note: Primary dark background and text-on-light. globals.css currently ships #08090E; #0C0E1A is canonical company-wide.

navy.note: Secondary dark surface; logomark structural fill on light backgrounds.

slate.note: Secondary text in light mode; source of the 20%-alpha dark-mode border.

silver.note: Secondary AND tertiary text on dark — both roles resolve here by design.

fog.note: Primary text on dark; borders and dividers on light.

cool-warm-fog.note: Logomark structural fill on dark. Deliberately warmer than Fog so the diamond reads as an object, not as text.

amber.note: The studio's own voice. Constant #D4933D on the logomark dot in both themes; deepens to #B8802E for interactive use on light.

gold.note: Amber's hover state in prose links. A highlight, never a fill.

crema.note: Sixteen to One. Inherited from that product's own coffee-derived kit.

tomato.note: Stockpot. Deliberately moved off coral to a true red so it cannot be confused with Amber or Crema.

vivid-violet.note: Bramble. The one product accent identical in both themes.

electric-cyan.note: Reviso. Falls back to Cyan Deep #06B6D4 on light backgrounds; Cyan Dark #0891B2 for text-on-white at WCAG AA.

display.purpose: Source Serif 4 Light. Exactly two uses site-wide: the homepage promise and Sixteen to One's name.

wordmark.purpose: Outfit 600 uppercase at +6px tracking. The VYTTLE lockup in nav and footer.

headline.purpose: Outfit 600. Page titles; app pages set it uppercase at +6px in the product accent.

title.purpose: Outfit 500. Section headings within a page.

body.purpose: DM Sans. All reading copy at line-height 1.8; taglines and support copy drop to 300.

field.purpose: DM Sans Light at 16px for form controls. 16px is a floor, not a preference — iOS Safari zooms the viewport when focusing an input below it.

micro.purpose: DM Sans 400 at 10px uppercase, +1.5px to +2px. Status badges and type chips. The smallest tier, and the one where contrast must be measured rather than assumed — every contrast failure this system has had was at this size.

label.purpose: DM Sans uppercase, 10-11px, +2px to +4px tracking. The most-used voice on the site.

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: Bento cell hover only. Emitted, not cast — zero offset.

shadows.name: mark-halo
shadows.purpose: App-page hero logomarks at rest. Makes the mark read as lit rather than printed.

shadows.name: menu-shadow
shadows.purpose: The nav Products dropdown. The single real drop shadow in the system.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: All hover and interaction state changes. No bounce, no overshoot.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal and page-load fade, translateY(12-16px) to 0, staggered 80ms per item.

motion.name: float
motion.purpose: Hero logomark, translateY 0 to -12px. Ambient, never demanding.

motion.name: pulse-dot
motion.purpose: Coming Soon badge dot, opacity 0.4 to 1.

motion.name: scroll-hint
motion.purpose: Homepage scroll cue, 6px vertical drift with opacity.

motion.name: aurora
motion.purpose: Eight independent atmosphere bands with staggered durations so the field never visibly loops.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid amber with Midnight text. Used only for the support form's submit — the site's single primary action. Dark-on-accent is required: white on amber is 2.6:1 and fails WCAG AA.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 1px; background: var(--amber, #D4933D); color: var(--midnight, #0C0E1A); padding: 14px 32px; border: none; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.2s ease, background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--gold, #F0D48A); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--amber, #D4933D); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Coming Soon Badge
components.description: Outlined pill with a pulsing accent dot. Marks a product that is real but not yet shipped.
components.css: .ds-badge-soon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--badge-bramble, #9D7AFF); border: 1px solid var(--badge-bramble, #9D7AFF); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 6px 16px; } .ds-badge-soon-dot { width: 5px; height: 5px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; animation: ds-pulse-dot 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse-dot { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.4; } 50% { opacity: 1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-badge-soon-dot { animation: none; opacity: 1; } }

components.name: Available Now Badge
components.description: Filled pill, inverted from Coming Soon. Text sets in the product's own dark background color — the inversion is what marks a shipped product.
components.css: .ds-badge-available { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; background: var(--crema, #C4956A); color: #1C1008; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 6px 16px; }

components.name: Bento Cell
components.description: The homepage product cell. Barely present at rest, roughly 3x more present on hover — the most characteristic interaction in the system.
components.html:
Mobile
Bramble

Contacts, untangled.
components.css: .ds-bento { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; padding: 32px; border-radius: 12px; text-decoration: none; overflow: hidden; background: color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 4%, var(--surface-glass, rgba(12,14,26,0.92))); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 10%, transparent); transition: transform 0.2s ease, background 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-bento:hover { transform: scale(1.02); background: color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 12%, var(--surface-glass, rgba(12,14,26,0.92))); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 25%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 40px color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 8%, transparent); } .ds-bento:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7C4DFF; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-bento-type { position: absolute; top: 24px; right: 24px; font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-tertiary, #A8ADBD); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #7C4DFF 25%, transparent); border-radius: 12px; padding: 3px 8px; } .ds-bento-mark { width: 48px; height: 48px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-bento-name { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text-primary, #DDE0E8); } .ds-bento-tagline { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text-secondary, #A8ADBD); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-bento { transition: none; } .ds-bento:hover { transform: none; } }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Support form text field. Stacked label above a translucent, hairline-bordered field. Never sets below 16px — iOS Safari zooms the viewport on focus below that.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-field-label { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 1px; color: var(--text-secondary, #A8ADBD); } .ds-field-input { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 300; font-size: 16px; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(91,97,120,0.2)); background: var(--bg-card, rgba(26,30,53,0.6)); color: var(--text-primary, #DDE0E8); width: 100%; transition: border-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: var(--text-secondary, #A8ADBD); opacity: 0.6; } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--amber, #D4933D); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, #D4933D 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Navigation Bar
components.description: Fixed 64px glass bar. The wordmark's +6px tracking is the single most recognizable typographic detail in the identity.
components.html:
VYTTLE
  • Products
  • Support
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; height: 64px; padding: 0 24px; background: var(--nav-bg, rgba(12,14,26,0.85)); backdrop-filter: blur(20px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(91,97,120,0.2)); } .ds-nav-brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-wordmark { font-family: var(--font-outfit), 'Outfit', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 6px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-primary, #DDE0E8); } .ds-nav-links { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 24px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .ds-nav-link { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: var(--text-secondary, #A8ADBD); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--amber, #D4933D); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--amber, #D4933D); outline-offset: 4px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: 36px circular icon button. Both themes are first-class, so this is a peer control, not a preference buried in a menu.
components.html: <button class="ds-theme-toggle" aria-label="Switch to light mode"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="5"/><path d="M12 1v2M12 21v2M4.22 4.22l1.42 1.42M18.36 18.36l1.42 1.42M1 12h2M21 12h2M4.22 19.78l1.42-1.42M18.36 5.64l1.42-1.42"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-theme-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(91,97,120,0.2)); background: transparent; color: var(--text-secondary, #A8ADBD); cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-theme-toggle:hover { color: var(--amber, #D4933D); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #D4933D 40%, transparent); } .ds-theme-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--amber, #D4933D); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Section Eyebrow
components.description: The wide-tracked uppercase micro-label that opens a section. The most-used typographic voice on the site.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { font-family: var(--font-dm-sans), 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 300; letter-spacing: 4px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-tertiary, #A8ADBD); }

narrative.overview:
A dark room built for watching small, precise things. The page is a near-black field with a slow aurora drifting far behind it; the content sits forward on glass, flat and exact. Nothing in this system competes for attention, because an observatory that glares at you is a failed observatory. The atmosphere moves on 6-10 second cycles and never resolves into a shape you can name. You look through it, not at it.

The instruments are the logomarks: hard geometry, even-odd cutouts, no flourish, no gradient, no bevel. The Vyttle diamond is a solid form with a circular hole punched through it and a single amber dot suspended in the gap. That amber dot is the fixed star — it is #D4933D in dark mode and #D4933D in light mode, in every size, forever. Every other color in this system is theme-aware. That one is not, and its constancy is the whole idea.

Five products share this sky, and each owns exactly one accent. Their colors never mix and never fill; they arrive as light — a 4% tint, a 10% border, a 40px glow on hover. Restraint here is measured, not vibed: a bento cell at rest is barely present, and hovering it roughly triples its presence. That 3x jump is the personality of the entire system.
keyCharacteristics: Two planes only: a fixed, blurred atmosphere and a flat content layer on glass
One accent per product, always emitted as light, never used as a large fill
Amber belongs to the studio alone and is constant across both themes
Geometric display type set in wide uppercase; humanist body type set light
Motion is ambient and slow; state changes are 200ms and never bounce
Dark is the default; both themes are fully designed, not inverted

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Amber is the studio's color, not a product's. A product page uses that product's accent for every accent role; it never borrows amber. Conversely, no product accent may appear on the homepage hero, the footer, or the wordmark. Nothing on this site uses two accents at once.

rules.name: The Constant Star Rule
rules.body: The amber dot at the center of the Vyttle diamond is #D4933D in every theme, every size, and every export. It is the only color in the system exempt from theming. If a mark's dot changes with the theme, the mark is wrong.

rules.name: The Emitted Color Rule
rules.body: Product accents arrive as light, not as paint: a 4% background tint, a 10% border, a 25% border and 40px glow on hover, a 1.5px hero outline. There are exactly two sanctioned solid fills in the system — the Available Now badge and the primary button — and both follow the same inversion: solid accent, dark text.

rules.name: The Dark-On-Accent Rule
rules.body: Any solid accent fill sets its text dark, never white. Every accent in this palette is mid-to-high lightness, so white-on-accent fails WCAG AA — amber measures 2.6:1 against white and 7.3:1 against Midnight. If a new component needs a solid accent background, the text is Midnight or that product's dark tone; if the design seems to demand white text, the fill is the wrong color.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Text Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two text tones per theme, not three. --text-secondary and --text-tertiary resolve to the same value (Silver on dark, Slate on light) because a third, fainter tone failed WCAG AA at the sizes this site uses it. Do not reintroduce a dimmer tier to create hierarchy; use size, weight, and tracking instead.

rules.name: The Wide Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text never sets below +2px tracking, and the smaller it gets, the wider it tracks: badges at 10px take +2px, section eyebrows at 11px take +4px, the wordmark at 16px takes +6px. Uppercase at default tracking is a bug in this system.

rules.name: The Serif Exception Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is not a general display face. It appears in exactly two places: the homepage promise and Sixteen to One's name. Adding a third use dilutes both. Every other heading is Outfit.

rules.name: The Light-Weight Rule
rules.body: Nothing on this site sets above 600, and body copy that wants to feel calm sets at 300. Weight is not how this system creates emphasis — color and tracking are.

rules.name: The 1200 Rule
rules.body: Content never exceeds 1200px, and text never exceeds its own narrower measure inside that. A full-width element on this site is always atmosphere, never content.

rules.name: The Two-Plane Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two planes: the atmosphere (fixed, blurred, aria-hidden) and the content (flat, on glass). Nothing lives between them. A new element that wants to feel raised is asking the wrong question — it belongs on the content plane, flat, and it distinguishes itself with tint and border.

rules.name: The Perceptual Parity Rule
rules.body: The atmosphere is tuned by eye, not by number. Light mode carries roughly twice the alpha of dark mode (0.35-0.45 versus 0.18-0.25) because color on white needs it to register at all. These numbers are supposed to disagree — matching them would destroy the parity they create. Dark is additionally dialed back so the bento cells' own accents are not masked.

rules.name: The Look-Through Rule
rules.body: The atmosphere must never become the subject. If a visitor notices the background before the words, it is too loud. It has no hard edges, resolves into no recognizable shape, and every band stays under blur(70px).

rules.name: The Glass-Not-Clear Rule
rules.body: A content surface sitting over the atmosphere composites onto --surface-glass (0.92 alpha), never onto transparent. The atmosphere belongs behind content, not behind text. A 96%-clear surface lets the aurora through the words themselves, and because the aurora animates, the effective contrast becomes a moving target — 10px labels measured as low as 1.3:1 against a light-mode band at peak. 0.90 is the measured floor; 0.92 is the token. Pair it with a backdrop blur so the surface reads as glass rather than as a panel.

rules.name: The Softer-As-It-Grows Rule
rules.body: Radius is proportional to surface: 10px for controls, 12px for cells, 24px for containers, pill for badges. A 24px radius on a button, or a 10px radius on a page-level container, breaks the scale.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: An instrument responds accurately; it does not perform. Transitions run 200ms for state and 400ms for theme, with no bounce, no spring, and no overshoot anywhere in the system.

dos: Do treat the atmosphere as something to look through. Keep it behind glass, aria-hidden, pointer-events: none, and under blur(70px).
Do give each product exactly one accent, inherited from that product's own brand kit, so the color matches its app icon and store listing.
Do express accents as light — 4% tint, 10% border, hover glow — and reserve solid accent fills for the Available Now badge alone.
Do keep the amber dot at #D4933D in both themes, at every size, in every export.
Do track uppercase wide: +2px minimum, +4px for 11px eyebrows, +6px for the wordmark.
Do design light mode as its own composition. Both themes are first-class; light is not an inversion, and its atmosphere is legitimately ~2x the alpha of dark's.
Do hold 32px of internal padding in bento cells and 1200px maximum content width.
Do keep transitions at 200ms for state and 400ms for theme, with no easing that overshoots.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion for every new animation, matching the existing block that disables fades, reveals, and decorative motion.
Do give policy, support, and per-app legal pages the same craft as the homepage — they carry more real traffic.
donts: Don't let this read as a generic AI-era SaaS landing page. The aurora is one wrong move from that cliche; what saves it is that it stays behind glass and never becomes the subject. No gradient blob behind a centered CTA, no testimonial wall, no Trusted by logo strip, no pricing table.
Don't let it read as an Apple product-page clone. No scroll-jacking, no parallax device reveals, no full-bleed hero screenshots, no spec-sheet drama.
Don't let a legal or support page read as a compliance page. No unstyled prose, no default blue links, no bare h1 on white.
Don't let it read as an indie-maximalist portfolio. No brutalist type, no chaotic grids, no novelty cursors. Personality here comes from precision, not volume.
Don't add a shadow to a resting surface. If something needs to come forward, it glows in its own accent or it moves to the nav's glass — those are the only two answers.
Don't introduce a third text tone to create hierarchy. Two tones per theme; use size, weight, and tracking instead.
Don't use amber on a product page or a product accent on the homepage hero, footer, or wordmark.
Don't set Source Serif 4 anywhere beyond the homepage promise and Sixteen to One's name.
Don't add analytics, embeds, remote fonts, or any third-party runtime request. The site's tracking-free implementation is the argument for its privacy claim.
Don't fabricate social proof. No testimonials, ratings, user counts, or download numbers exist.
